slot.brief: Give volumes and molarities of an acid and a base (with clear stoichiometry like HCl vs NaOH) and ask for the volume of one needed for complete neutralisation of the other.

stem: What volume of $0.30\ \text{M}$ KOH is needed to completely neutralise $30\ \text{mL}$ of $0.20\ \text{M}$ $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$?

verdicts.working: Moles of H₂SO₄ = 0.030 × 0.20 = 0.006 mol. Neutralisation requires 2 mol KOH per mol H₂SO₄, so V(KOH) = (0.012 mol)/(0.30 mol L⁻¹) = 0.040 L = 40 mL.

working:
$\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4 + 2\text{KOH} \rightarrow \text{K}_2\text{SO}_4 + 2\text{H}_2\text{O}$
$n(\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4)=0.20\times30=6.0\ \text{mmol}$
$n(\text{KOH})=2\times6.0=12.0\ \text{mmol}$
$V(\text{KOH})=12.0/0.30=40\ \text{mL}$

Independent check: Moles of H₂SO₄ = 0.030 × 0.20 = 0.006 mol. Neutralisation requires 2 mol KOH per mol H₂SO₄, so V(KOH) = (0.012 mol)/(0.30 mol L⁻¹) = 0.040 L = 40 mL.
solution:
The reaction is $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4+2\text{KOH}\rightarrow\text{K}_2\text{SO}_4+2\text{H}_2\text{O}$, so $2$ mol of KOH neutralise $1$ mol of $\text{H}_2\text{SO}_4$.
$$V_{\text{KOH}}=\frac{2(0.20)(30)}{0.30}=40\text{ mL}$$
